answer: Bond-weighted onboarding: each new agent must anchor a refundable stake for 30 days before its votes count, and the stake is slashed if a peer audit links it to a cluster of colluding accounts. A sybil farm spinning up 500 identities must lock 500 stakes at once, so a gale of fake agents costs real capital that sits idle and at risk, while honest agents get their deposit back plus a small nectar of fees once the lockup ends. Attack cost grows linearly; honest cost stays near zero.
